findings.title: Data race on shared variables in errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Inside group.Go, `totalBatchesIndexed++` and the assignment `_, _, err = s.build(...)` write to the outer `err` and counter from concurrent goroutines (SetLimit allows initWorkers>1). This is a data race. Errors can be lost or overwritten, and the reported count can be wrong. Now that init runs at startup, this runs on every boot. Use a local err and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Blocking Init in constructor runs with a never-cancelled context and can block startup
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, which builds all search indexes and calls lifecycle hooks (e.g. backend DB init). Any failure makes server construction fail and blocks startup for the whole index build. The previous lazy behaviour tolerated a slow or failed init. The test is skipped for postgres, which suggests it already breaks. The context is the long-lived server ctx, so Stop cancelling it will only be seen after Init finishes.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without lock
findings.body: BuildIndex now writes b.cache under cacheMu only briefly and concurrently, and TotalDocs ranges over the map with no lock. With concurrent builds (and now init calls TotalDocs for logging right after), this can cause a concurrent map iteration and write fatal error. Take cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Concurrent builds of same key are no longer serialized
findings.body: Removing the function-wide lock lets two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key (e.g. getOrCreateIndex from Search and handleEvent, both seeing a nil index) run simultaneously. For file-backed indexes, bleve.New on the same directory will fail for the second caller. For memory indexes, the last writer silently overwrites the cached index. Dedupe per key instead.
